newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks hit 31-month high, Tokyo up slightly.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks hit 31-month high, Tokyo up slightly.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks, boosted by futures-led buying, closed at a 31-month high on Friday, while Tokyo rose moderately after a fourth consecutive day of gains.

Elsewhere, Bombay shares lost 1.58 percent on fears of looming political instability but Thailand's bourse gained on speculative buying before Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa announced he would dissolve parliament and call a snap election on November 17.

Brokers said buyer activity ahead of the expiry of September Hang Seng futures this session pushed the key Hang Seng index 123.26 points, or 1.06 percent, higher to 11,759.39, after hitting a 1996 intra-day high at 11,788.41
It was the highest close since February 1994.
"Futures-related buying has been positive. The bulls have had more say than the bears," said Andrew Fernow, director of research at Vickers Ballas.
September Hang Seng futures rose 115 points to 11,733.
Analysts said investors were encouraged by the decline in the U.S. long bond yield. The long bond rose 17/32 on Thursday, pushing the yield down to 6.89 percent.
Tokyo stocks managed only small gains after a three-day winning run.
The key 225-share Nikkei average rose 85.65 points, or 0.40 percent, to close at 21,547.02. But the key December futures were down 50 points to finish at 21,500.

Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's dissolution of the Lower House of parliament earlier in the day and his cabinet's formal announcement of October 20 for general elections had been widely expected by market participants, brokers said.

"The dissolution of parliament itself had no impact. If there were to be any, it would depend on the structure of the next government," said Koji Asano, senior manager of foreign exchange at Fuji Bank.
Bombay's 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index fell 52.32 points, or 1.58 percent, to a provisional 3,254.73.
"The political uncertainty has heightened," said Bharat Iyer, strategist at UBS Securities. "This is the reason for the fall (in share prices) over the last two days."
He said the market was trying to discount the possible arrest of former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, whose Congress party's support is crucial for the minority coalition government.
Bangkok's SET index gained 5.15 points, or 0.49 percent, to 1,047.95.
Banharn's decision to dissolve parliament came after trading finished and on the eve of a deadline to quit his job.
The market has been sluggish since Banharn announced last Saturday that he would quit within seven days in return for support in a no-confidence vote in parliament.
The Australian share market closed higher, extending its run to four consecutive positive finishes.
The All Ordinaries index ended up 9.6 points, or 0.42 percent, at 2,283.
Taiwan and Seoul markets are closed until Monday for national holidays.
At 1131 GMT, the dollar was at 110.70/80 yen and 1.5228/38 marks.
Bullion ended at US$380.70/381.20, against New York's US$380.90/381.40 close on Thursday.
SIMEX North Sea Brent crude oil futures for November were slightly lower. November Brent last traded at $22.86 a barrel, down seven cents from London's close.
